html:
The legend of Abla Pokou, an Akan princess who, in the 18th century, led her followers west out of the Asante kingdom after a succession fight, and founded the Baoule people in what is now central Ivory Coast.

Tradition says that when the Comoe River blocked their escape, she gave her infant son to the river and the waters let them pass; the name Baoule is said to mean "the child is dead". The story is taught in every Ivorian school. The Baoule settled the savanna around Bouake and Sakassou and became the largest single group in the country, and Houphouet-Boigny was a Baoule chief. See also the Akan peoples.
